svg.title: The RAG pipeline: an offline indexing lane and an online querying lane
svg.desc: A hand-drawn two-lane pipeline. The upper lane, indexing, runs once per document: raw documents such as PDFs, wikis, code, tickets, and transcripts are chunked by structure, sentence, parent-child, or late chunking; embedded with a contextual prefix; and stored in a vector index alongside a BM25 index. A dashed line carries that index down to the lower lane. The lower lane, querying, runs on every turn: a user query is retrieved against by hybrid vector and BM25 search for about twenty candidates, a cross-encoder reranks them down to the best three to five, and those are augmented into the RAG layer of the context before the model is called. Captions note that chunk size and splitter choice decide more of the outcome than the vector database does, and that a manifest table is what makes index drift answerable.
svg.text: RAG, from raw documents to a grounded answer
Two lanes. The offline one runs once per document; the online one runs on every user turn.
the index the online lane reads
Vanilla RAG. Chunk size and splitter choice decide more of the outcome than the vector database does.
Advanced patterns — HyDE, Self-RAG, CRAG, GraphRAG — rewrite or loop the querying lane. See Posts 09 and 17.
A manifest table with a row per source document is what makes "what changed in the index since last week" answerable.
